goal: Resolve P1 security vulnerabilities (XSS in AdminLogisticsPage.tsx) and optimize performance (N+1 query resolution in stock-alert Edge Function).
constraints: Must preserve the visual aesthetics of the AdminLogisticsPage.
Must ensure full backward-compatibility for Edge Functions and page components.
known_context: The AdminLogisticsPage.tsx processes tracking number text inputs raw without dynamic sanitation. The stock-alert Edge Function fetches alert recipients inside a loop for each low stock product, generating redundant database queries.

risks.description: XSS sanitization in input field might accidentally truncate valid tracking numbers if characters are too restricted.
Edge function caching of recipients could fail if inventory settings change mid-run (highly unlikely to affect correct alerts).

options.title: Strict input-level alphanumeric dynamic sanitization and pre-submit payload filtering
options.reason: This guarantees that no malicious character is ever processed or saved to the DB, preventing both stored and DOM-based XSS cleanly.

options.title: Edge-Function-only sanitization
options.reason: While safe for backend, it still allows un-sanitized states on the client-side which is vulnerable to DOM-based XSS.

recommendation: Option A is selected because input-level dynamic sanitization combined with pre-submit payload sanitization provides double-layered security.

traces.finding: Found that updateRow updates state tracking_number directly from event value and handleBulkSubmit uses tracking_number directly without regex sanitization.
Found that processProductAlert queries getAlertRecipients (which makes a database query to inventory_settings) in every iteration of the loop over all low stock products.
